title: Action Approval Grant
description: An approval bound to the fingerprint of one action (adoption area A2). Adopted from keryx's policy engine property: an approval authorizes exactly one action, bound to that action's fingerprint, and a single-use grant is spent once consumed. Two kinds exist: an 'operator' grant (single-use, minutes) and a 'standing' grant held by an autonomous actor (not consumed, bounded by being narrow). The first and only adopter in scope is the restart family.

grantId.description: Opaque, unguessable identifier. This is what travels in callback data; the action never travels with it (P-5.4).

requestId.description: The pending request this grant answers. Null for a standing grant, which answers no single request.

issuedAt.description: When the grant came into existence — the FIRST tap of the two-tap confirmation, not the confirming tap. The unconsumed grant is itself the pending state.

expiresAt.description: For an 'operator' grant: minutes — a restart approval is answered immediately or not at all. For a 'standing' grant: null, because it is revoked rather than expired.

consumedAt.description: Set when an 'operator' grant is spent; once set it authorizes nothing further (P-2.2). A 'standing' grant is never consumed — that exemption is what 'standing' means — and every use is instead recorded as an autonomous action so the operator can see in the morning what restarted itself.

oneOf.description: Telegram user id of the sender who approved. Used when kind is 'operator'.

actor.description: The autonomous actor holding the grant.

authorizedBy.description: Telegram user id of the operator who authorized the standing grant. A standing grant still has a human behind it.

issuedBy.description: Who the grant belongs to. Per-sender authorization means the identity of the approver is part of the record, not an assumption about the room.

statedTo.description: The human sentence shown to the operator before they answered — the words the grant's 'да' refers to. Recorded so that a disputed restart can be reconstructed from what was actually asked, not from what the code meant.

kind.description: An 'operator' grant is single-use and short-lived: one press, one action. A 'standing' grant belongs to an autonomous actor (today only scripts/tmux-watchdog.ts), is not consumed on use, and is bounded by being narrow rather than by being temporary. Decided 2026-08-12: without it, P-2.3 would turn a 4am recoverable hang into an outage until morning.

actionFingerprint.description: Deliberately coarse. A fingerprint over the exact command string would re-ask on every trivial variation and train the operator to approve without reading — which is the failure being prevented, reached by a different road. These three components are what the operator would actually notice.

half.description: Which half of the system the action restarts. The exact distinction the recorded incidents turned on: containers are the bot and Postgres; sessions are the tmux windows and their channel subprocesses. Code that ships in the container does not reach a running session.

scope.description: 'all', an absolute project path, or 'container:<name>' for a single named container. A one-project restart is not a stack restart, and one named container is not the container half.

downtime.description: Whether the operator loses the running session, and for how long. 'brief' means it comes back on its own; 'full' means it stays down until something else brings it up — which is why tmux_stop and proj_stop are 'full'.

examples.statedTo: Перезапустить только контейнер бота. Сессии останутся на старом коде.
tmux-watchdog may restart a wedged session of this project without asking. It may not restart the container, the whole stack, or another project.
